el: Read every question aloud and point to the pictures or objects. Let students answer by pointing, showing with counters or saying the number.
Keep a number line, ten frames and a picture word wall (add, take away, more, less, equal) on the desk.
Read word problems aloud on request; reading is not the skill being tested. Pre-teach key words such as each, total, left, area, equal parts.
Offer sentence frames for written answers: "I know ___ because ___." "First I ___, then I ___."
Allow a bilingual glossary of math terms. Pre-teach academic words (ratio, rate, expression, inequality, proportional).
Accept answers that mix English and the home language when the math reasoning is clear, and accept labeled diagrams as part of an explanation.
Allow a bilingual glossary and read word problems aloud on request. Give a sentence frame for justification: "This works because ___, so ___."
iep: Give the assessment in small groups or one to one, with manipulatives available. Split into two short sittings if needed.
Extended time (1.5x), items read aloud, multiplication chart or calculator only where the IEP allows and the item is not testing that fact.
Extended time, fewer items per page, a reference sheet of formulas, and a calculator where the IEP allows.
Extended time, a formula sheet, graph paper, and a calculator where the IEP allows. Let students dictate written explanations.

el: Read every item aloud, more than once if needed. Use picture cards for vocabulary and let students answer orally or by pointing.
Accept home-language responses for comprehension; reading in English is the skill only on foundational (phonics) items.
Pre-teach 3 to 5 key words from each passage with pictures. Allow a bilingual dictionary on reading items, not on vocabulary items.
Give sentence frames for written answers: "The author says ___. I know because the text says ___."
Allow a bilingual glossary of literary terms (theme, claim, evidence, tone). Offer a paragraph frame (claim, evidence, explanation) for written responses.
Provide a word bank of academic vocabulary for the unit and allow students to plan writing in their home language before drafting in English.
iep: Assess one to one or in a small group. Use larger print and break the assessment into two short sittings.
Extended time, passages read aloud on comprehension items, graphic organizer for writing, speech-to-text where the IEP allows.
Extended time, chunked passages with fewer items per page, a planning organizer, and speech-to-text where the IEP allows.
Extended time, text-to-speech for passages, an outline template for essays, and reduced length on the performance task where the IEP allows.

el: Use real objects, photos and hands-on demonstrations. Read items aloud and accept answers by pointing, drawing or speaking in any language.
Pre-teach science words with pictures (for example, force, habitat, energy). Provide sentence frames for explanations: "I observed ___. This shows ___."
Provide a bilingual science glossary and labeled diagrams. Offer a claim-evidence-reasoning frame for written answers.
Provide a word bank of key terms, allow labeled diagrams as part of explanations, and read data-heavy items aloud on request.
iep: Assess one to one through hands-on tasks; allow drawing or oral answers instead of writing.
Extended time, read-aloud of text and graphs, a vocabulary card, and the option to dictate written explanations.
Extended time, fewer items per page, a formula or vocabulary reference sheet, and graphic organizers for CER responses.
Extended time, calculator and formula sheet where allowed, read-aloud of data tables, and chunked performance tasks.

el: Use photos, maps with pictures and real objects. Read items aloud and accept answers by pointing, drawing or speaking in any language.
Pre-teach key terms with visuals (for example, mission, colony, government). Provide sentence frames: "This source shows ___ because ___."
Provide a bilingual glossary, annotated maps and timelines. Offer a claim-evidence-reasoning frame and allow notes in the home language.
Provide a word bank of academic and historical terms, read primary sources aloud on request, and allow graphic organizers for essays.
iep: Assess one to one or in a small group with hands-on maps and pictures; allow drawing or oral answers.
Extended time, read-aloud of sources and questions, a timeline or map reference, and dictation for written answers.
Extended time, chunked primary sources with fewer items per page, and a graphic organizer for document-based writing.
Extended time, text-to-speech for documents, an essay outline template, and reduced document sets where the IEP allows.

math|-1.about: Transitional kindergarten follows the Eureka Math Pre-Kindergarten modules: counting to 5 and then to 10 and 20, naming shapes and position words, comparing length, weight, capacity and groups, and acting out simple addition and subtraction stories with real objects. Items are short and meant to be read aloud; objects are described in words.
std: Recite numbers in order to 20 and count up to 10 objects, saying one number for each object; the last number tells how many.
Recognize and name numerals 0 to 10 and match them to groups of objects.
Compare two groups of up to 5 objects by matching and counting and tell which has more, fewer or the same.
Understand that adding to or taking away from a group changes the number; act out and solve simple stories within 5.
Sort and classify objects by one attribute, such as color, size or kind.
Compare two objects by length, weight or capacity using words such as longer, heavier and holds more.
Identify, describe and build shapes, including circles, triangles, squares, rectangles, spheres, cubes and cylinders.
Describe where objects are using position words such as above, below, next to, in front of and behind.

units.name: Module 1: Counting to 5
units.el: Use real objects for every item and accept number words in the child's home language. Post numeral cards 1 to 5 with matching dots.

practice.q: Which one does not belong? apple, banana, grape, car
practice.h: Three of them are foods you can eat.

practice.q: Which one goes with a toothbrush?
practice.h: Think about what you use when you brush your teeth.

practice.q: Sort the blocks by color: red, blue, red. How many red blocks?
practice.h: Touch each red block and say one number for each.

practice.q: Count the cats: cat cat cat. How many cats?
practice.h: Point to each cat one time as you count.

practice.q: How many noses do you have?
practice.h: Touch your nose and count.

practice.q: Show 2 fingers. Then show 3 fingers. (Teacher watches.)
practice.ans: Holds up 2 fingers, then 3 fingers, and says the number each time.

quiz.q: Which one does not belong? sock, shoe, hat, banana
Which one goes with a pillow?
Count the birds: bird bird. How many birds?
How many wheels does a bike have?
Leaves: green, green, yellow, green. How many green leaves?
Count the spoons on the table: spoon spoon spoon. How many spoons?
Ana has 1 shoe on. How many more shoes does she need to make a pair?
Sort 6 buttons or blocks into 2 groups. Tell how you sorted them.
quiz.ans: Makes two groups by one attribute (such as color or size) and names the rule, for example "red ones and blue ones."

practice.q: Count the ducks: duck duck duck duck. How many ducks?
practice.h: Touch each duck once. The last number you say tells how many.

practice.q: Count the fingers on one hand. How many fingers?
practice.h: Wiggle each finger as you count it.

practice.q: Count the dots: o o o o o. How many dots?
practice.h: Move your finger from left to right and say one number for each dot.

practice.q: Kim counts 4 apples in a line. Then she counts them starting at the other end. How many apples now?
practice.h: Did any apples get added or taken away?

practice.q: Which group has 4?
practice.h: Count each group and stop when you find 4.

practice.q: Count out 5 counters from a big pile and push them to the teacher.
practice.ans: Takes exactly 5 counters, touching each once, and stops at 5.

quiz.q: Count the stars: star star star star star. How many stars?
How many legs does a dog have?
Count the cars: car car car car. How many cars?
4 children sit in a circle. The teacher counts them starting with a different child. How many children now?
Count the claps: clap clap clap clap clap. How many claps?
Leo counts his toy trucks: 1, 2, 3, 4. How many trucks does he have?
Which number do we say after 4?
Show 4 on your fingers two different ways.
quiz.ans: For example, 4 fingers on one hand, and 2 fingers on each hand (or 3 and 1).

practice.q: Which numeral shows three?
practice.h: Think about the number you say after 2.

practice.q: Count the hats: hat hat. Which numeral matches?
practice.h: Count first, then find that numeral.

practice.q: Count the balls: ball ball ball ball ball. Which numeral matches?
practice.h: Say one number for each ball, then find the numeral you said last.

practice.q: A card has the numeral 4. Put that many cubes on it. How many cubes?
practice.h: Read the numeral, then count out cubes until you say that number.

practice.q: Which one is a numeral, not a letter?
practice.h: Numerals tell how many. Letters make sounds.

practice.q: Trace the numerals 1, 2 and 3 in sand or on paper. Say each one.
practice.ans: Traces each numeral with the correct shape and names it.

quiz.q: Which numeral shows one?
Count the cups: cup cup cup cup. Which numeral matches?
Which number word goes with the numeral 5?
A box has the numeral 3 on it. How many crayons should go in the box?
Count the frogs: frog frog frog frog frog. How many frogs?
Sam put 2 blocks on the card with the numeral 3. What should he do?
Which numeral do we say first when we count?
The teacher holds up numeral cards 1 to 5 out of order. Name each one.
quiz.ans: Names all five numerals correctly.

lessons.name: One more and numbers in order

practice.q: What number comes after 3?
practice.h: Count 1, 2, 3 out loud. What do you say next?

practice.q: You have 2 grapes. You get 1 more. How many grapes now?
practice.h: Show 2 fingers, then put up 1 more.

practice.q: A tower has 4 cubes. Add 1 more cube. How many cubes now?
practice.h: One more is the next number when you count.

practice.q: Which number is missing? 1, 2, __, 4, 5
practice.h: Say the numbers in order and listen for the gap.

practice.q: Stairs made of cubes: 1 cube, 2 cubes, 3 cubes. What step comes next?
practice.h: Each step has one more cube than the step before.

practice.q: Build towers of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 cubes. Put them in order from short to tall.
practice.ans: Builds the five towers and lines them up 1 to 5; each tower is one cube taller than the one before.

quiz.q: There is 1 fish in a bowl. Dad adds 1 more fish. How many fish now?
Which number comes right before 5?
Count with me: 3, 4, ... What comes next?
A tower has 3 cubes. Ming adds 1 more. How many cubes are in the tower?
Ana has 4 stickers. Her friend gives her 1 more. How many stickers now?
Which group is 1 more than 2 bears?
Which list is in counting order?
You have 3 blocks. Tell what happens when you add 1 more.
quiz.ans: I have 4 blocks. One more makes the next counting number.

test.q: Which one does not belong? dog, cat, fish, spoon
Which one goes with a bowl of soup?
Blocks: blue, blue, red, blue, red. How many red blocks?
Count the bees: bee bee bee. How many bees?
Count the balls: ball ball ball ball. How many balls?
Count the hearts: heart heart heart heart heart. How many hearts?
How many eyes do you have?
Which numeral shows four?
Count the shells: shell shell. Which numeral matches?
What number comes after 2?
Which number is missing? 2, 3, __, 5
Mia counts 5 dolls. She moves them into a circle and counts again. How many dolls now?
A plate has the numeral 4 on it. How many crackers go on the plate?
Joe has 3 toy cars. He gets 1 more car. How many cars now?
There are 2 kids on the slide. 1 more kid climbs on. How many kids are on the slide?
Grandma bakes 4 muffins. Then she bakes 1 more. How many muffins now?
Which tower is 1 cube taller than a tower of 3 cubes?
Lena counted her blocks like this: 1, 2, 3, 5. What mistake did she make?
You need 5 cups for 5 friends. You have 4 cups. How many more cups do you need?
Count out 4 counters and put the numeral card 4 next to them.
test.ans: Takes exactly 4 counters with one-to-one counting and chooses the numeral 4.

test.q: Sort a small pile of buttons into two groups. Tell your sorting rule and how many are in each group.
test.ans: Sorts by one attribute (color, size or number of holes), states the rule and counts each group (up to 5) correctly.

test.q: Why does the last number you say tell how many? Tell or show with blocks.
test.ans: When I count, I say one number for each block, so the last number I say is how many blocks there are.

test.q: Give the child 8 small toys and numeral cards 1 to 5. Ask the child to (1) count out 3 toys, (2) count out 5 toys in another group, (3) match each group with its numeral card, and (4) add 1 more toy to the group of 3 and say how many now.
rub: Counts out both groups exactly, matches both numerals, and says 4 for one more without recounting from 1.
Counts and matches both groups; recounts from 1 to find one more.
Counts or matches only one group correctly, or makes one or two counting errors.
Cannot yet count out a group of 3.

units.name: Module 2: Shapes
units.el: Keep a basket of real shapes (plates, boxes, cans, balls). Have children point and repeat each shape name and position word with a gesture.

practice.q: Which shape is round and has no corners?
practice.h: Trace the edge with your finger. Does it ever turn a corner?

practice.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
practice.h: Count the straight sides with your finger.

practice.q: A cookie is shaped most like which shape?
practice.h: Think about the edge of a round cookie.

practice.q: A yield sign on the road has 3 straight sides. What shape is it?
practice.h: How many sides does it have?

practice.q: Count the corners on a triangle. How many corners?
practice.h: A corner is where two sides meet.

practice.q: Find something in the room shaped like a circle. Tell how you know.
practice.ans: Points to a round object, such as a clock or plate, and says it is round with no corners.

quiz.q: Which shape has 3 corners?
A coin is shaped most like which shape?
A slice of pizza is shaped most like which shape?
How many corners does a circle have?
Which is NOT a triangle?
Which shape is the sun drawn as in most pictures?
Sara puts 3 sticks together to close a shape. What shape did she make?
How is a circle different from a triangle?
quiz.ans: A circle is round with no sides or corners. A triangle has 3 straight sides and 3 corners.

practice.q: Which shape has 4 sides that are all the same length?
practice.h: Measure each side with your finger. Are they all the same?

practice.q: A door is shaped most like which shape?
practice.h: A door is tall and has 4 sides.

practice.q: How many sides does a rectangle have?
practice.h: Trace each side and count.

practice.q: A cracker has 4 sides, all the same length. What shape is it?
practice.h: Look at the sides. Are they all the same?

practice.q: Which shape has 4 corners?
practice.h: Count the corners on each shape.

practice.q: Make a square with 4 craft sticks. Show the teacher.
practice.ans: Uses 4 equal sticks and closes the shape with 4 corners.

quiz.q: Which shape is long with 4 sides?
How many corners does a square have?
A book cover is shaped most like which shape?
Which shape has 4 sides, with 2 long sides and 2 short sides?
Which shape is a window in a building most often?
Max made a shape with 4 sticks that are all the same. What did he make?
Count the sides of a picture frame shaped like a square. How many sides?
How are a square and a rectangle the same?
quiz.ans: Both have 4 straight sides and 4 corners.

practice.q: A ball is shaped like a
practice.h: Is it flat or can you hold it all around?

practice.q: A block with 6 flat square faces is a
practice.h: Think of a toy block or a number cube.

practice.q: A can of soup is shaped like a
practice.h: It is round on the top and bottom and stands up.

practice.q: Which shape can roll?
practice.h: Try rolling each one in your mind. Which has no flat sides?

practice.q: Which shape can stack on top of another one like it?
practice.h: Stacking works best with flat sides.

practice.q: Find something in the room shaped like a cube. Tell how you know.
practice.ans: Points to a box or block and says it has flat square faces.

quiz.q: An orange is shaped most like a
A paper towel roll is shaped like a
A number cube for a game is shaped like a
Which shape can roll and also stand flat?
A gift box with all square faces is shaped like a
Which is flat?
Pedro stacks 3 cubes into a tower. Then he adds 1 more cube. How many cubes are in the tower now?
How is a ball different from a circle drawn on paper?
quiz.ans: The ball is a solid sphere you can hold and roll. The circle is flat.

practice.q: The cat sleeps under the table. Where is the cat?
practice.h: "Under" means lower than something.

practice.q: The bird sits on top of the house. Where is the bird?
practice.h: Is the bird high or low?

practice.q: In line, Mia stands first and Jay stands right after her. Where is Mia?
practice.h: Who is at the front of the line?

practice.q: The ball is between two chairs. How many chairs does it touch on its sides?
practice.h: "Between" means in the middle of two things.

practice.q: You need 3 sticks to make a triangle. How many sticks do you need for 1 triangle and 1 more stick?
practice.h: Count 3 sticks, then 1 more.

practice.q: Put a block next to your chair, then on your chair, then under your chair. Say a position word each time.
practice.ans: Places the block correctly each time and says "next to," "on" and "under."

quiz.q: The lamp is beside the bed. Which word means the same as beside?
The toys are in the box. Where are the toys?
A rug is on the floor under the table. What is above the rug?
Kai is behind Lin in line. Who is in front?
Rosa uses 4 straws to make a square. How many straws does she use?
The moon is high in the sky. The house is on the ground. The moon is ___ the house.
Which pieces can make a square?
ch: 4 sticks that are the same length

quiz.q: Tell where your shoes are right now. Use a position word.
quiz.ans: Uses a position word correctly, for example "My shoes are on my feet" or "under the table."

test.q: Which shape has 3 sides?
Which shape has no corners?
Which shape has 4 sides that are all the same?
A dinner plate is shaped most like which shape?
A soccer ball is shaped like a
A toy block with 6 square faces is a
A juice can is shaped like a
A sandwich cut corner to corner makes two halves. Each half is shaped like a
A rug is long with 4 sides and 4 corners. The long sides are longer than the short sides. What shape is it?
How many corners does a rectangle have?
Count the sides of a triangle. How many sides?
Ben made 2 triangles with sticks. Each triangle has 3 sticks. How many sticks did he use?
The dog is under the bed. Where is the bed?
Ava is first in line. Leo is behind Ava. Who is in front?
The pencil is in the cup. Where is the pencil?
Which shape will roll down a ramp?
Which shape is flat?
Tess says a square is not a rectangle because it is not long. Which is true?
ch: a square has 4 sides and 4 corners too

test.q: Sort: ball, box, orange, block. Which ones are shaped like a sphere?
Point to something in the room shaped like a rectangle.
test.ans: Points to a door, book, table top or window and names it as a rectangle.

test.q: How is a cube different from a square?
test.ans: A cube is solid and can be held; it has 6 square faces. A square is flat.

test.q: Put a toy above, below and next to a box. Say the position word each time.
test.ans: Places the toy correctly each time and says "above," "below" and "next to."

test.q: Give the child a bag of flat shapes (circle, triangle, square, rectangle) and solid shapes (ball, block, can). Ask the child to (1) sort the shapes into flat and solid, (2) name at least 4 shapes, (3) tell how a triangle and a square are different, and (4) put the ball next to the can.
rub: Sorts correctly, names 4 or more shapes, tells a clear difference (3 sides and 4 sides) and follows the position direction.
Sorts correctly and names 3 shapes; the difference is unclear.
Sorts with some errors or names 1 or 2 shapes.
Cannot yet sort or name shapes.

units.name: Module 3: Counting to 10
units.el: Use a 10-bead counting string and finger counting. Say each number word with the child, and let them count first in their home language.

practice.q: Count the apples: apple apple apple apple apple apple. How many apples?
practice.h: Touch each apple once. The last number you say is how many.

practice.q: Count the dots: o o o o o o o. How many dots?
practice.h: Count slowly from left to right.

practice.q: Show 5 fingers on one hand and 1 on the other. How many fingers?
practice.h: Start at 5 and count 1 more.

practice.q: Which number comes after 6?
practice.h: Count 1 to 6 out loud, then say the next number.

practice.q: There are 7 days in a week. Count them: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun. How many days?
practice.h: Put up one finger for each day.

practice.q: Count out 6 crayons and put them in a cup.
practice.ans: Counts out exactly 6 crayons, one number for each crayon.

quiz.q: Count the shoes: shoe shoe shoe shoe shoe shoe. How many shoes?
Count the trees: tree tree tree tree tree tree tree. How many trees?
A ladybug has 3 spots on one wing and 3 on the other. How many spots?
Which number comes before 7?
Mom puts 5 grapes on a plate, then 2 more. How many grapes?
Nia counted 7 rocks in a row. She counts them in a circle. How many rocks now?
Which group has 6?
Show 7 on your fingers.
quiz.ans: Holds up 7 fingers, for example 5 on one hand and 2 on the other.

practice.q: Count the boats: boat boat boat boat boat boat boat boat. How many boats?
practice.h: Point to each boat as you count.

practice.q: How many fingers do you have on two hands?
practice.h: Count each finger once.

practice.q: Count the drums: drum drum drum drum drum drum drum drum drum. How many drums?
practice.h: Touch and count. Do not skip any.

practice.q: A spider has 8 legs. Which number shows how many legs?
practice.h: Count by putting up one finger for each leg.

practice.q: There are 10 crayons in a box. How many crayons?
practice.h: Count each crayon once.

practice.q: Count 10 jumps out loud while you jump.
practice.ans: Says 1 to 10 in order with one number for each jump.

quiz.q: Count the balloons: balloon balloon balloon balloon balloon balloon balloon balloon balloon. How many balloons?
How many toes do you have on two feet?
Which number comes after 8?
Count the bowls: bowl bowl bowl bowl bowl bowl bowl bowl. How many bowls?
An egg carton has 2 rows of 5 eggs. How many eggs?
Sam counts his blocks: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. How many blocks does he have?
Which number comes right before 10?
Count out 8 counters. Then line them up and count again. Is it still 8? Why?
quiz.ans: Yes. Moving the counters does not add or take any away, so there are still 8.

practice.q: There are no cookies on the plate. How many cookies?
practice.h: What number means none?

practice.q: Which numeral shows eight?
practice.h: Eight is the number after seven.

practice.q: Count the pens: pen pen pen pen pen pen. Which numeral matches?
practice.h: Count first, then find that numeral.

practice.q: A card shows the numeral 10. How many beads go on it?
practice.h: 10 is the number of fingers on two hands.

practice.q: A bag has the numeral 7. Put that many marbles inside. How many marbles?
practice.h: Read the numeral, then count marbles to that number.

practice.q: The teacher shows numeral cards 0 to 10 out of order. Name each one.
practice.ans: Names at least 9 of the 11 numerals correctly.

quiz.q: Which numeral means none?
Which numeral shows nine?
Count the bugs: bug bug bug bug bug bug bug. Which numeral matches?
The bus has 0 children on it. Then 1 child gets on. How many children are on the bus?
All 3 birds fly away from a tree. How many birds are left in the tree?
Which numeral is more than 8?
Which numeral card goes with ten fingers?
Write or trace the numeral 0 and tell what it means.
quiz.ans: Writes 0 and says it means none or nothing.

lessons.name: One more and counting in order to 10

practice.q: What number is 1 more than 6?
practice.h: Say 6, then the next number.

practice.q: Which number is missing? 6, 7, __, 9, 10
practice.h: Count from 6 and listen for the gap.

practice.q: Lucy has 8 beads on a string. She adds 1 more. How many beads now?
practice.h: Start at 8 and count 1 more.

practice.q: A tower has 9 cubes. Add 1 more. How many cubes now?
practice.h: What number comes after 9?

practice.q: Which list is in counting order?
practice.h: Say the numbers from 6 to 10 out loud.

practice.q: Build a cube stair from 1 to 10. Point to the step with 7 cubes. What number is 1 more than 7?
practice.ans: Builds the stair in order, points to the 7 step and says 8 is one more.

quiz.q: There are 5 kids in a line. 1 more kid joins. How many kids now?
What number comes after 9?
Which number is missing? 3, 4, 5, __, 7
Which is 1 more than 7 bears?
Ray has 9 toy cars. He gets 1 more for his birthday. How many cars does he have now?
Count backward: 10, 9, 8, ... What comes next?
Ana counts: 5, 6, 7, 9, 10. Which number did she skip?
You have 6 stickers. Your friend gives you 1 more. Tell how many you have and how you know.
quiz.ans: I have 7. One more than 6 is the next number when I count.

test.q: Count the fish: fish fish fish fish fish fish. How many fish?
Count the lamps: lamp lamp lamp lamp lamp lamp lamp. How many lamps?
Count the cookies: cookie cookie cookie cookie cookie cookie cookie cookie cookie cookie. How many cookies?
Count the pears: pear pear pear pear pear pear pear pear. How many pears?
Which numeral shows seven?
There are no fish in the bowl. Which numeral tells how many fish?
What number comes after 7?
Which number is missing? 7, 8, __, 10
Count the clouds: cloud cloud cloud cloud cloud cloud cloud cloud cloud. Which numeral matches?
Jun has 2 hands. How many fingers does he have?
A bag has the numeral 6 on it. How many apples go in the bag?
Dad sets the table with 7 forks. He adds 1 more fork for Grandpa. How many forks now?
There are 4 frogs on a log and 4 frogs in the grass. How many frogs?
Sofia counts 9 buttons in a pile. She spreads them out and counts again. How many buttons now?
Count backward: 5, 4, 3, ... What comes next?
Which group has 1 more than 9 stars?
Eli counted 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8. What mistake did he make?
You have 9 crackers. There are 10 children. How many more crackers do you need so each child gets 1?
All 5 birds fly off the fence. How many birds are on the fence now?
Count out 9 counters for the teacher.
test.ans: Takes exactly 9 counters with one number for each counter.

test.q: Show the numeral card that matches 10 fingers and tell how you know.
test.ans: Picks the card 10 and says there are 10 fingers on two hands, or counts them.

test.q: Line up 8 blocks. Count them. Then put them in a pile. How many now? Why?
test.ans: 8. No blocks were added or taken away, so the number stays the same.

test.q: Give the child numeral cards 0 to 10, a cup of 15 counters and a cube stair from 1 to 10. Ask the child to (1) count out 7 counters and put the 7 card next to them, (2) show what is 1 more than 7, (3) find the card for zero and say what it means, and (4) count from 1 to 10 out loud.
rub: Counts out 7 exactly, says 8 for one more without recounting, explains 0 as none and counts to 10 with no errors.
Does 3 of the 4 parts correctly.
Does 1 or 2 parts correctly.
Cannot yet count out a group of 7.

units.name: Module 4: Comparison of length, weight, capacity and numbers to 5
units.el: Model the comparison words with gestures (arms wide for longer, hands sinking for heavier) and real objects. Post picture cards for longer, shorter, heavier, lighter, more, fewer and same.

practice.q: A pencil and a crayon start at the same line. The pencil sticks out farther. Which is longer?
practice.h: Line up the ends. Which one goes past the other?

practice.q: A snake and a worm lie side by side. The snake is much longer. Which is shorter?
practice.h: Shorter means it does not reach as far.

practice.q: Two ribbons start at the same place and end at the same place. What is true?
practice.h: Look at both ends.

practice.q: Which is taller, a giraffe or a cat?
practice.h: Think about which one could reach a tree top.

practice.q: To compare two sticks, what should you do first?
practice.h: Fair comparing starts at the same place.

practice.q: Find something in the room that is longer than your shoe.
practice.ans: Lines up the object with the shoe and shows that it reaches farther.

quiz.q: A bus and a car park in a row. The bus is longer. Which is shorter?
Which is longer, a broom or a spoon?
Zoe stands next to her dad. Her head comes up to his belt. Who is taller?
Two straws start at the same line. One ends past the other. The one that ends past is

math|0.about: Kindergarten follows the Eureka Math Kindergarten modules: counting and writing numbers to 10, naming and describing flat and solid shapes, comparing lengths, weights, capacities and numbers, finding number pairs and solving addition and subtraction stories within 10, understanding teen numbers as ten ones and some more ones, counting to 100, and building and composing shapes. Items are short and meant to be read aloud.
std: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; the last number said tells how many, and each next number is one more.
Count to answer "how many?" questions about as many as 20 things in a line, array or circle, or 10 things scattered.
Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than or equal to the number in another group.
Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, and record each with a drawing or equation.
Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones.
Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes using informal language to describe their parts and attributes.

units.name: Module 3: Comparison of length, weight, capacity and numbers to 10
units.el: Teach the comparing words in pairs with gestures: longer/shorter, taller/shorter, heavier/lighter, more/fewer/less. Use the frame "The ___ is ___ than the ___."

math|1.about: First grade follows the Eureka Math Grade 1 modules: sums and differences to 10, making ten and taking from ten within 20, measuring and comparing lengths with units, place value and comparison to 40 and then to 100, adding two-digit numbers, describing, composing and partitioning shapes, and telling time to the half hour. Items are short and meant to be read aloud.
std: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems with unknowns in all positions, using objects, drawings and equations.
Add and subtract within 20, fluently within 10, using strategies such as counting on, making ten and decomposing a number leading to ten.
Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers.
Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones.
Compare two two-digit numbers based on the tens and ones digits, recording the results with >, = and <.
Add within 100 using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, including adding a two-digit number and a one-digit number or a multiple of 10.
Express the length of an object as a whole number of same-size length units laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares and describe them as halves, fourths and quarters.

units.name: Module 1: Sums and differences to 10
units.el: Use number bond drawings (a whole and two parts) every day. Post the story frames "___ and ___ make ___" and "___ take away ___ is ___," and act out word problems with objects before writing equations.

practice.q: Which two parts make the whole 7?
practice.h: Put the parts together. Do they make 7?

practice.q: Count on to solve: 6 + 3 = ?
practice.h: Start at 6 and count 3 more: 7, 8, 9.

practice.q: A number bond has the whole 9 and one part 5. What is the other part?
practice.h: What do you add to 5 to make 9?

practice.q: There are 8 cubes. 5 are blue and the rest are red. How many are red?
practice.h: Count on from 5 to 8.

practice.q: To add 2 + 7, which is the fastest way to count on?
practice.h: Start with the bigger number.

practice.q: Draw a number bond for 10 with two parts. Then write two addition sentences for it.
practice.ans: Example: whole 10, parts 6 and 4; 6 + 4 = 10 and 4 + 6 = 10.

quiz.q: Which two parts make the whole 6?
Count on to solve: 5 + 4 = ?
A number bond has the whole 10 and one part 7. What is the other part?
Lena has 9 pencils. 6 are yellow and the rest are green. How many are green?
Which shows counting on to find 8 + 2?
Which number bond is NOT correct?
Explain how counting on from the bigger number helps you solve 2 + 6.
quiz.ans: Start at 6 and count 2 more: 7, 8. That is faster than counting all 8 from 1.

lessons.name: Addition word problems and switching the order

practice.q: Marco has 4 toy dinosaurs. He gets 5 more for his birthday. How many dinosaurs does he have now?
practice.h: Draw 4, then 5 more, or count on from the bigger number.

practice.q: There are 3 red apples and 6 green apples in a bowl. How many apples are in the bowl?
practice.h: Put the two groups together.

practice.q: If you know 3 + 5 = 8, what else do you know?
practice.h: Switching the order of the parts does not change the total.

practice.q: Which story matches 2 + 6 = 8?
practice.h: Look for a story where two groups go together.

practice.q: Kim reads 2 books on Monday and 7 books on Tuesday. How many books does she read?
practice.h: Add the two days together.

practice.q: Write a word problem that 4 + 6 = 10 could solve.
practice.ans: Example: I have 4 stickers and get 6 more. How many now? 10 stickers.

quiz.q: Five kids are playing tag. 3 more kids join. How many kids are playing now?
There are 2 bluebirds and 7 robins in a tree. How many birds are in the tree?
Which has the same total as 1 + 8?
Jaden has 6 cars. His sister gives him 4. How many cars does he have?
Sara says 6 + 2 and 2 + 6 have different totals. What is true?
Which equation matches: 5 pears and 5 more pears?
Draw a picture for this story and write an equation: 7 ducks swim and 2 more come.
quiz.ans: Picture of 7 ducks and 2 more; 7 + 2 = 9.

practice.h: Count up from 4 to 7.

practice.q: Which addition sentence helps you solve 9 - 6?
practice.h: What part do you add to 6 to make 9?
Start at 5 and count up to 8.
What number plus 2 makes 6?
Think 7 + ? = 10.

practice.q: Explain how 4 + 5 = 9 helps you solve 9 - 5.
practice.ans: 9 is the whole and 5 is one part, so the other part is 4. 9 - 5 = 4.

quiz.q: Which addition fact helps solve 10 - 4?
Ana needs 10 beads. She has 8. How many more beads does she need?
Which equation is true?
Leo says 7 - 3 = 5. Explain his mistake using addition.

practice.q: There are 9 cupcakes. The class eats 4. How many cupcakes are left?
practice.h: Start with 9 and take away 4.

practice.q: Abby had 10 balloons. Some popped. Now she has 7. How many popped?
practice.h: Count up from 7 to 10.

practice.q: There are 8 kids. 5 are wearing jackets. How many are NOT wearing jackets?
practice.h: The whole is 8 and one part is 5.

practice.q: Rami picks 6 flowers. He gives 6 to his mom. How many does he have left?
practice.h: What happens when you take away all of them?

practice.q: Which equation matches: 7 frogs, 2 hop into the pond?
practice.h: Hopping away means taking away.

practice.q: Write a subtraction story for 10 - 6 and solve it.
practice.ans: Example: 10 kids were on the bus and 6 got off. 4 kids are still on the bus.

quiz.q: There are 7 goldfish in a tank. 3 are moved to another tank. How many goldfish are in the first tank now?
Lucia had some crayons. She gave away 2 and now has 6. How many did she have at first?
There are 9 seats on the bus. 6 are taken. How many seats are empty?
Which story matches 8 - 3?
Ten kids are at the park. 4 go home. Which equation tells how many are left?
Dev has 5 grapes. He eats some and has 1 left. How many did he eat?
Solve and explain: 9 birds sat on a wire. Some flew away. 5 are still on the wire. How many flew away?
quiz.ans: 4 birds flew away. 5 + 4 = 9, so 9 - 5 = 4.

practice.q: Is 5 + 2 = 7 true or false?
practice.h: Solve the left side and compare.

practice.q: Which equation with 4 + 4 is true?
practice.h: Find the total on each side of the equal sign.
Count back 2 from 9.
Think of the pairs that make 10.

practice.q: Which number makes 3 + 5 = ? + 4 true?
practice.h: First find 3 + 5. Then what plus 4 is that number?

practice.q: Is 7 = 10 - 3 true? Explain how you know.
practice.ans: True. 10 - 3 is 7, so both sides are the same.

quiz.q: Is 6 + 1 = 8 true or false?
Which way to make 9 is true?
Which number makes 2 + 6 = ? + 7 true?
Which equation with 5 + 5 is false?
Ty says 4 + 3 = 7 + 2 is true because they both have a 7. Is he right? Explain.
quiz.ans: No. 4 + 3 is 7, but 7 + 2 is 9. The two sides are not the same, so it is false.

test.q: Which two parts make the whole 9?
A number bond has the whole 8 and one part 2. What is the other part?
Which addition fact helps solve 7 - 5?
Which has the same total as 3 + 6?
Which equation with 6 + 3 is true?
Which number makes 4 + 4 = ? + 3 true?
Maya has 6 shells. She finds 3 more at the beach. How many shells does she have now?
There are 10 kids on the playground. 7 go inside. How many kids are still on the playground?
Theo had 5 stickers. He got some more. Now he has 9. How many stickers did he get?
A box has 8 crayons. 2 are broken. How many crayons are not broken?
Which story matches 10 - 3?
Rosa says 8 - 3 = 11. What mistake did she make?
Jin had some marbles. He gave 4 to his brother and has 5 left. How many marbles did Jin have at first?
Which way to make 7 is false?
Draw a number bond for 7. Write two addition and two subtraction sentences that go with it.
test.ans: Example: whole 7, parts 4 and 3; 4 + 3 = 7, 3 + 4 = 7, 7 - 3 = 4, 7 - 4 = 3.

test.q: Explain how you can use 6 + 4 = 10 to solve 10 - 6.
test.ans: 10 is the whole and 6 is one part, so the other part is 4. 10 - 6 = 4.

test.q: Write a word problem for ? + 3 = 8 and solve it.
test.ans: Example: I had some cookies. Mom gave me 3 more. Now I have 8. How many did I have? 5.

test.q: The class has 10 snack bags. 4 bags have pretzels and the rest have apple slices. (1) How many bags have apple slices? Draw a number bond. (2) 3 kids eat their apple slices. How many apple slice bags are left? (3) Write an equation for each part and explain how you know your answers are right.
rub: Correct answers 6 and 3, a number bond with whole 10 and parts 4 and 6, equations 10 - 4 = 6 (or 4 + 6 = 10) and 6 - 3 = 3, and a clear check.
Both answers correct with equations; the explanation or number bond is incomplete.
One part correct, or a correct plan with one calculation error.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 2: Introduction to place value through addition and subtraction within 20
units.el: Use two ten frames and a 10-stick of linking cubes. Say teen numbers both ways ("thirteen" and "1 ten 3 ones") and use the frames "Make ten, then add ___" and "Take from ten, then add ___."

practice.q: To solve 9 + 4, Ana makes ten. Which shows her thinking?
practice.h: How many does 9 need to make 10? Break 4 into that number and the rest.
Move 1 from the 5 to make 10, then add the rest.
8 needs 2 to make 10. Break 6 into 2 and 4.

practice.q: 8 + 5 is the same as 10 + ?
practice.h: 8 takes 2 from the 5 to make 10. What is left of the 5?

practice.q: Jack has 9 toy trains. He gets 7 more. How many trains does he have?
practice.h: Make ten with the 9 first.

practice.q: Show how to make ten to solve 7 + 5. Draw or write your steps.

quiz.q: 9 + 8 is the same as 10 + ?
Which shows making ten for 8 + 4?
There are 7 kids on the slide and 6 kids on the swings. How many kids in all?
Pablo scores 9 points, then 9 more points. How many points does he score?
Explain why 9 + 3 is the same as 10 + 2.
quiz.ans: 9 gets 1 from the 3 to make 10, and 2 are left, so 9 + 3 = 10 + 2 = 12.

practice.q: To solve 13 - 9, Ben takes 9 from the ten. Which shows his thinking?
practice.h: Break 13 into 10 and 3. Subtract 9 from the 10.
Take 9 from 10, then add the 2 ones.
10 - 8 = 2. Then add the 5 ones.

practice.q: 14 - 9 is the same as 1 + ?
practice.h: 10 - 9 leaves 1. Add back the ones from 14.

practice.q: There are 16 muffins. The class eats 9. How many muffins are left?
practice.h: Take 9 from the 10, then add the 6.

practice.q: Show how to take from ten to solve 11 - 7.

quiz.q: 13 - 8 is the same as 2 + ?
Noor has 15 stickers. She gives 7 to a friend. How many stickers does Noor have left?
There were 12 eggs. 8 were used for breakfast. How many eggs are left?
Which way shows taking from ten for 16 - 9?
Explain why 12 - 9 = 3 by taking from ten.
quiz.ans: 12 is 10 and 2. Take 9 from 10 to get 1, then add the 2 ones: 1 + 2 = 3.

lessons.name: Teen numbers as tens and ones

practice.q: How many tens and ones are in 17?
practice.h: A ten is a group of 10. How many are left over?

practice.q: What number is 1 ten 4 ones?
practice.h: Start at 10 and add the ones.
1 ten and 9 ones.

practice.q: Which shows 12?
practice.h: 12 is 1 ten and some ones.

practice.q: A pack has 10 juice boxes. Eva has 1 pack and 6 loose juice boxes. How many juice boxes does she have?
practice.h: 1 ten and 6 ones.

practice.q: Draw 15 using a ten-stick and ones. Write it as tens and ones.
practice.ans: A 10-stick and 5 cubes; 1 ten 5 ones.

quiz.q: What number is 1 ten 8 ones?
How many ones are in 13 after you make a ten?
20 is how many tens?
A bag holds 10 marbles. Kai has 1 full bag and 9 loose marbles. How many marbles?
Which is the same as 1 ten 1 one?
Zoe says 16 has 6 tens. What is right?
Explain what the 1 in 14 means.
quiz.ans: The 1 means 1 ten, or 10 ones. 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones.

practice.q: Liam has 8 red blocks and 7 blue blocks. How many blocks does he have?
practice.h: Make ten with the 8.

practice.q: There were some birds on a roof. 5 flew away. Now there are 9. How many birds were on the roof at first?
practice.h: Put back the birds that flew away.

practice.q: Hana has 13 grapes. Ken has 9 grapes. How many more grapes does Hana have than Ken?
practice.h: Count up from 9 to 13.

practice.q: Sofia picks 4 red flowers, 6 yellow flowers and 3 white flowers. How many flowers does she pick?
practice.h: Look for two numbers that make 10 first.

practice.q: Which equation matches: 11 kids, some go home, 4 are left?
practice.h: Start with 11. Some go away. 4 stay.

practice.q: Solve and explain: Omar has 6 cars. He needs 15 for his race track. How many more cars does he need?
practice.ans: 9 more cars. 6 + 4 = 10, and 5 more is 15, so 4 + 5 = 9.

quiz.q: There are 9 apples in a basket and 8 on the table. How many apples are there?
Mia has 16 beads. She uses 7 on a bracelet. How many beads are left?
Ravi has 5 more books than Tia. Tia has 8 books. How many books does Ravi have?
A class has 7 boys, 3 girls with glasses and 5 girls without glasses. How many kids are in the class?
Gina has 12 stickers. Ben has 8. Which equation tells how many fewer Ben has?
Some ducks were in a pond. 6 more came. Now there are 14. How many ducks were there at first?
Which equation helps solve 9 + ? = 16?
Lucy says 4 + 7 + 6 is easier if you add 4 + 6 first. Is she right? Explain.
quiz.ans: Yes. 4 + 6 = 10, and 10 + 7 = 17. Making ten first makes it easier, and the order does not change the total.

test.q: What number is 1 ten 5 ones?
How many tens and ones are in 19?
9 + 6 is the same as 10 + ?
Which shows taking from ten for 14 - 9?
Which equation helps solve 8 + ? = 15?
Isla has 9 pennies. She finds 5 more. How many pennies does she have?
There are 17 kids in the pool. 9 get out. How many kids are still in the pool?
Some kids are reading. 7 more kids join them. Now 12 kids are reading. How many kids were reading at first?
Alex has 6 crackers, 4 cheese slices and 5 grapes on his plate. How many pieces of food are on his plate?
Nina has 18 shells. Owen has 9. How many more shells does Nina have?
Sam solved 8 + 5 like this: 8 + 2 = 10, then 10 + 2 = 12. What mistake did he make?
ch: he added 2 again instead of the 3 left

test.q: Which is the same as 7 + 6?
Show how to make ten to solve 9 + 8.
test.ans: 9 + 1 = 10, and 7 more makes 17. So 9 + 8 = 17.

test.q: Draw 16 with a ten-stick and ones. Tell what the 1 and the 6 mean.
test.ans: A 10-stick and 6 cubes. The 1 means 1 ten and the 6 means 6 ones.

test.q: Write a word problem for 12 - ? = 5 and solve it.
test.ans: Example: I had 12 balloons and some floated away. 5 are left. How many floated away? 7.

test.q: The class is planting a garden. Mr. Diaz has 9 tomato plants and 8 bean plants. (1) How many plants does he have? Show how you made ten. (2) He plants 11 of them on Monday. How many are left to plant? Show how you took from ten or counted up. (3) His goal is 20 plants. How many more plants does he need to buy? Explain your thinking with equations.
rub: Correct answers 17, 6 and 3, with making ten shown (9 + 1 + 7), a clear subtraction strategy (17 - 11 = 6) and an equation for the goal (17 + 3 = 20).
All three answers correct; one strategy is not shown clearly.
One or two answers correct, or correct strategies with a calculation error.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 3: Ordering and comparing length measurements as numbers
units.el: Practice the words longer, longest, shorter, shortest, taller and length with real objects and gestures. Use the frame "The ___ is ___ cubes long. It is ___ cubes longer than the ___."

practice.q: A rope is longer than a stick. The stick is longer than a pencil. Which is longest?
practice.h: Put them in order from shortest to longest.

practice.q: Three ribbons: red is longest, blue is shortest. Where does green go?
practice.h: The green one is not the longest or the shortest.

practice.q: A door is taller than Mia. Mia is taller than a chair. What is true?
ch: the door is taller than the chair
the chair is taller than Mia
the chair is taller than the door
Mia is taller than the door
practice.h: Use Mia to compare the door and the chair.

practice.q: A paper strip is as long as a desk. The strip is shorter than a rug. What is true?
ch: the desk is shorter than the rug
the desk is longer than the rug
the desk and rug are the same
practice.h: The strip is the same as the desk, so compare the strip to the rug.

practice.q: Order from shortest to longest: bus, bike, car.
practice.h: Which is the smallest? Which is the biggest?

practice.q: Use a string to compare the length of your desk and the door width without moving them. Tell which is longer.
practice.ans: Cuts or marks the string to match one length, holds it against the other, and says which is longer.

quiz.q: A hose is longer than a jump rope. The jump rope is longer than a shoelace. Which is shortest?
Ali is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Cora. Who is the shortest?
A string is the same length as a table. The string is longer than a bookshelf. What is true?
ch: the table is longer than the bookshelf
the bookshelf is longer than the table

quiz.q: Order from longest to shortest: pencil, paper clip, ruler.
Which is taller, a giraffe or a horse?
To compare two objects that cannot be moved, what can you use?
ch: a string cut to the length of one

quiz.q: A blue snake is 6 cubes long. A green snake is 9 cubes long. How many cubes long is the longer snake?
Explain why you must line up the ends when you compare two pencils.
quiz.ans: If the ends do not start at the same place, a shorter pencil could look longer. Lining up the ends makes the comparison fair.

practice.q: A pencil is measured with cubes laid end to end. It is as long as 8 cubes. How long is the pencil in cubes?
practice.h: Count the cubes from one end to the other.

practice.q: Joy measured a book with paper clips but left gaps. What will happen?
ch: her number will be too small
her number will be too big
practice.h: Gaps mean some of the length was not covered.

practice.q: Raj measured with cubes that overlap. What should he do?
ch: lay the cubes end to end
practice.h: Units should touch but not overlap.

practice.q: Kim used 3 big blocks and 2 small cubes to measure a shoe. Why is this not a good measure?
ch: the units are not the same size
she should use more big blocks
practice.h: All units should be the same size.

practice.q: A crayon is 5 cubes long. Two crayons are placed end to end. How many cubes long are they together?
practice.h: Add the length of each crayon.

practice.q: Measure a glue stick with centimeter cubes. Tell how long it is and how you measured.
practice.ans: Lays cubes end to end from one end of the glue stick to the other with no gaps or overlaps and tells the number, such as 9 centimeters.

quiz.q: A spoon is as long as 7 paper clips laid end to end. How many paper clips long is the spoon?
Which way of measuring is correct?
ch: cubes end to end with no gaps

quiz.q: Ty measured his desk with his hand and got 6 hands. Zoe got 8 hands. Why are the numbers different?
A marker is 12 centimeter cubes long. A pencil is the same length. How long is the pencil in centimeters?
Why do people use centimeters to measure?
ch: everyone's centimeter is the same size

quiz.q: A worm is 4 cubes long. It grows 3 more cubes long. How long is it now?
Which tool would give the same answer for everyone?
Leo started measuring a ribbon from the middle of the first cube. Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: The first cube must start right at the end of the ribbon. Starting in the middle makes the measurement wrong.

practice.q: A green pencil is 9 cm long. A red pencil is 6 cm long. How much longer is the green pencil?
practice.h: Count up from 6 to 9.

practice.q: Ana's ribbon is 12 cubes long. Ben's ribbon is 8 cubes long. How much shorter is Ben's ribbon?
practice.h: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one.

practice.q: A key is 5 cm. A spoon is 13 cm. Which equation tells how much longer the spoon is?
practice.h: Find the difference between the two lengths.

practice.q: A train of cubes is 7 cubes long. Mia adds 6 more cubes. How long is it now?
practice.h: Add the new cubes to the length.

practice.q: A worm is 4 cm. A snake is 15 cm. A caterpillar is 9 cm. Which is longest?
practice.h: Compare the numbers.

practice.q: A blue crayon is 8 cm. A yellow crayon is 2 cm longer. How long is the yellow crayon? Explain.
practice.ans: 10 cm. 2 cm longer means add 2: 8 + 2 = 10.

quiz.q: A notebook is 16 cm long. A sticky note is 7 cm long. How much longer is the notebook?
Kai's paper strip is 11 cubes long. Jen's strip is 3 cubes shorter. How long is Jen's strip?
A carrot is 14 cm long. Mom cuts off 5 cm. How long is the carrot now?
Lengths: eraser 4 cm, glue 9 cm, scissors 13 cm. Order from shortest to longest.
A ribbon is 10 cubes. A string is 10 cubes. What is true?
A pencil is 8 cm. A marker is 5 cm longer. How long is the marker?
Tom says a 9 cm stick is longer than a 12 cm stick because 9 is a big number. What is true?
Explain how you find how much longer one object is than another.
quiz.ans: Measure both with the same unit, then subtract the smaller number from the bigger number or count up from the smaller to the bigger.

practice.q: A class votes for a pet: dog 7, cat 5, fish 2. How many kids voted for dog or cat?
practice.h: Add the dog and cat votes.

practice.q: A tally chart shows apples 8 and bananas 3. How many more kids chose apples?
practice.h: Subtract the smaller number from the larger.

practice.q: Favorite color: red 6, blue 9, green 4. Which color got the most votes?
practice.h: Find the biggest number.

practice.q: Weather this month: sunny 12 days, rainy 4 days, cloudy 3 days. How many days in all?
practice.h: Add all three numbers. Look for an easy pair to add first.

practice.q: Snack votes: chips 5, fruit 5, crackers 2. What is true?
ch: chips and fruit got the same votes
practice.h: Compare each pair of numbers.

practice.q: Ask 10 classmates if they like apples or oranges better. Make a tally chart and tell which won and by how many.
practice.ans: Tally chart with totals that add to 10, the winner named, and the difference found (for example 7 - 3 = 4).

quiz.q: Favorite sport: soccer 9, basketball 6, tennis 3. How many kids voted?
How many more kids chose soccer than tennis? Soccer 9, basketball 6, tennis 3.
Favorite sport: soccer 9, basketball 6, tennis 3. Which sport got the fewest votes?
Lunch choices: tacos 8, pasta 8, soup 1. Which is true?
Shoes in class: 7 with laces, 9 with straps, 2 slip-on. How many fewer slip-on shoes than shoes with straps?
A chart shows: books read by Ana 5, by Ben 4. Together, how many books did they read?
A tally chart shows 10 kids walk to school and 6 kids ride the bus. How many more kids walk?
Pets in class: dog 6, cat 4, none 7. Write a question that can be answered with this data and answer it.
quiz.ans: Example: How many kids have a pet? 6 + 4 = 10 kids.

test.q: A broom is longer than a bat. The bat is longer than a spoon. Which is shortest?
Pia is taller than Leo. Leo is taller than Sam. Who is tallest?
A string is as long as a rug. The string is shorter than the hallway. What is true?
ch: the rug is shorter than the hallway
the rug is longer than the hallway

test.q: Order from shortest to longest: ant, mouse, dog.
Which way of measuring a desk with units is correct?
ch: units end to end with no gaps or overlaps

test.q: Two kids measure the same table with their feet and get different numbers. Why?
A book is as long as 11 centimeter cubes. How long is the book in centimeters?
A green ribbon is 15 cm long. A pink ribbon is 9 cm long. How much longer is the green ribbon?
A lizard is 7 cm long. A snake is 9 cm longer than the lizard. How long is the snake?
Ivan's cube train is 13 cubes long. He takes off 4 cubes. How long is it now?
Lengths: crayon 8 cm, ruler 15 cm, paper clip 3 cm. Which is longest?
A pencil is 10 cm and a marker is 14 cm. Which equation tells how much longer the marker is?
Favorite fruit: apple 6, grape 8, pear 3. How many kids voted?
Favorite fruit: apple 6, grape 8, pear 3. How many more kids chose grape than pear?
Favorite fruit: apple 6, grape 8, pear 3. Which fruit got the most votes?
Rosa measured a shoe with cubes and got 9. She left a gap between two cubes. Is the shoe really longer or shorter than 9 cubes?
Jake's pencil is 2 cm longer than Amy's. Amy's pencil is 12 cm. Ella's pencil is 1 cm shorter than Jake's. How long is Ella's pencil?
Votes: blue 7, red 7, yellow 4. What is true?
Explain why everyone should use the same size unit when they measure.
test.ans: So everyone gets the same number for the same object. Different-size units give different numbers.

test.q: A tally chart shows 5 kids like rain and 12 kids like sun. Write two things the chart tells you.
test.ans: Example: More kids like sun. 7 more kids like sun than rain. 17 kids voted in all.

test.q: Ali says his 8-cube tower is longer than Mei's 11-cube tower because he built it on a table. Explain who is right.
test.ans: Mei's tower is longer. It has 11 cubes and Ali's has 8, so Mei's is 3 cubes longer. Where the tower stands does not change its length.

test.q: Give students 3 classroom objects (for example a pencil, a marker and a book) and centimeter cubes. (1) Measure each object and record its length. (2) Order the objects from shortest to longest. (3) Find how much longer the longest object is than the shortest. (4) Make a chart of your results and write one question someone could answer with it.
rub: Accurate lengths (within 1 cube) with no gaps or overlaps, correct order, correct difference with an equation, and a clear chart and question.
All parts done with one small error.
Measures correctly but the order, difference or chart is missing or wrong.
Little correct measuring.

units.name: Module 4: Place value, comparison, addition and subtraction to 40
units.el: Use 10-sticks and loose cubes for every number. Teach the symbols with words: > "is greater than," < "is less than," = "is equal to," and read each comparison aloud together.

practice.q: What number is 3 tens 4 ones?
practice.h: The tens come first, then the ones.

practice.q: How many tens are in 27?
practice.h: Look at the first digit.

practice.q: 2 tens 9 ones = ?
practice.h: 20 and 9 more.

practice.q: Which shows 31?
practice.h: 31 has 3 tens and 1 one.

practice.q: Dad buys 3 packs of 10 pencils and 6 loose pencils. How many pencils does he buy?
practice.h: Count the tens first: 10, 20, 30. Then count on the ones.

practice.q: Draw 25 using tens and ones. Write it as tens and ones.
practice.ans: 2 ten-sticks and 5 cubes; 2 tens 5 ones.

quiz.q: What number is 1 ten 9 ones?
How many ones are in 38?
4 tens 0 ones = ?
Which is the same as 23?
A teacher has 2 boxes of 10 crayons and 8 loose crayons. How many crayons does she have?
Which number has 3 tens and 0 ones?
Lia says 32 is 2 tens 3 ones. What is right?
Explain why the 2 in 26 is worth more than the 6.
quiz.ans: The 2 means 2 tens, which is 20. The 6 means 6 ones. 20 is more than 6.

practice.q: Which is greater, 29 or 32?
practice.h: Compare the tens first.

practice.q: Which symbol makes 17 ___ 21 true?
practice.h: Is 17 less than or greater than 21?

practice.q: Which comparison of 35 and 31 is true?
practice.h: Both have 3 tens. Compare the ones.

practice.q: Which number is less than 24?
practice.h: Look for a number with fewer tens, or the same tens and fewer ones.

practice.q: Ana has 26 stickers. Kim has 1 ten and 9 ones. How many stickers does the one with fewer have?
practice.h: Write Kim's number first, then compare.

practice.q: Compare 38 and 33 using >, < or =. Explain how you know.
practice.ans: 38 > 33. Both have 3 tens, and 8 ones is more than 3 ones.

quiz.q: Which is less, 16 or 13?
Which symbol makes 30 ___ 3 tens true?
Which comparison of 22 and 27 is true?
Order from least to greatest: 31, 13, 23
Raj read 34 pages. Eli read 3 tens 7 ones pages. How many pages did the one who read more read?
Which number is greater than 2 tens 8 ones?
Kai says 19 > 21 because 9 is bigger than 1. What is true?
Explain why you compare the tens first.
quiz.ans: Tens are worth more than ones. A number with more tens is greater, no matter how many ones it has (up to 9).

lessons.name: Ten more, ten less and adding tens

practice.q: What is 10 more than 14?
practice.h: Add one ten. The ones stay the same.

practice.q: What is 10 less than 33?
practice.h: Take away one ten. The ones stay the same.
2 tens and 1 ten.
Count by ten from 25.

practice.q: Lin has 17 marbles. She gets a bag of 10 more. How many marbles now?
practice.h: One more ten.

Write a word problem that can be solved with 3 x 4. Solve it.
quiz.ans: There are 3 vases with 4 flowers in each. How many flowers? 3 x 4 = 12 flowers.

practice.q: An array has 4 rows of 3 stars. Which equation matches?
practice.h: Count the number in each row, then count the rows.
Think: 3 times what number equals 27?

practice.q: Explain how an array of 3 rows of 6 can also show 6 rows of 3.
practice.ans: Turning the array gives 6 rows of 3. The total does not change: 3 x 6 = 6 x 3 = 18.

quiz.q: Which is the same as 2 x 9?
A garden has 3 rows with 8 carrots in each row. How many carrots?
Twins share 14 marbles equally. How many marbles does each twin get?
An array shows 18 dots in 3 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?
Use the commutative property to explain why knowing 3 x 8 helps you find 8 x 3.
quiz.ans: The commutative property says the order of factors does not change the product, so 8 x 3 = 3 x 8 = 24.

lessons.name: Multiplication and division with units of 4

practice.h: Count by 4s to 32. How many 4s did you count?

practice.q: A table has 4 legs. How many legs do 7 tables have?
Explain how doubling helps you multiply by 4. Use 4 x 7 as an example.
practice.ans: 4 is double 2. 2 x 7 = 14, and double 14 is 28, so 4 x 7 = 28.

quiz.q: Which number makes 4 x ? = 40 true?
A coach puts 28 players into teams of 4. How many teams are there?
Which array shows 4 x 5?
Each car has 4 wheels. How many wheels are on 9 cars?
Lily says 4 x 6 = 22. Explain her mistake and give the correct answer.
quiz.ans: 4 x 6 means 4 groups of 6. 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24, so the answer is 24, not 22.

lessons.name: Distributive property and word problems with 2 to 5 and 10

practice.q: Which shows 5 x 7 broken apart with the distributive property?
practice.h: Break 7 into 5 and 2. Multiply each part by 5.

practice.q: Sam buys 3 packs of 10 stickers and 2 more stickers. How many stickers does he have?
practice.h: First find 3 x 10, then add the 2 extra stickers.

practice.q: Use 5 x 8 = 40 to find 6 x 8. Explain your thinking.
practice.ans: 6 x 8 is one more group of 8 than 5 x 8, so 40 + 8 = 48.

quiz.q: Which equals 4 x 9?
A bakery sells muffins in boxes of 5. Mia buys 6 boxes and eats 3 muffins. How many muffins are left?
Ben has 40 cards. He puts them in rows of 10. How many rows does he make?
There are 3 rows of 10 chairs and 1 row of 5 chairs. How many chairs are there?
Explain two different ways to solve 6 x 5.
quiz.ans: Skip count by 5 six times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Or 5 x 5 = 25 plus one more 5 is 30.

test.q: Which equation shows 6 groups of 2?
What is 3 x 6?
Which situation can be solved with 20 / 4?
An array has 5 rows of 4 hearts. How many hearts are there?
Which number makes ? x 3 = 24 true?
Which is equal to 3 x 7?
Which shows 4 x 8 using the distributive property?
Jada has 5 vases with 4 roses in each. How many roses does she have?
36 students are split into 4 equal teams. How many students are on each team?
A box holds 10 crayons. How many crayons are in 7 boxes?
Kai puts 27 shells into 3 equal piles. Which equation finds the shells in each pile?
Which statement is true?
ch: 2 x 9 has the same product as 3 x 6

test.q: A store has 4 shelves with 6 toy cars on each shelf. It sells 5 cars. How many cars are left?
Ana reads 5 pages each day for 8 days. Leo reads 3 pages each day for 10 days. How many more pages does Ana read than Leo?
Draw an array for 3 x 5 and write a division equation that matches it.
test.ans: 3 rows of 5 dots; 15 / 3 = 5 or 15 / 5 = 3.

test.q: Write a word problem for 24 / 4. Tell whether your answer is the number of groups or the number in each group.
test.ans: 24 muffins in boxes of 4: how many boxes? 6 boxes, which is the number of groups.

test.q: Explain how you can use 5 x 6 = 30 to solve 4 x 6.
test.ans: 4 x 6 is one group of 6 less than 5 x 6, so 30 - 6 = 24.

test.q: The class is planning a picnic. Juice boxes come in packs of 4 and sandwiches come in trays of 5. There are 20 students and 4 adults, and each person gets 1 juice box and 1 sandwich. How many packs of juice and trays of sandwiches should the class buy? Show your work with equations and explain how you know there is enough for everyone.
rub: 24 people: 6 packs of juice (24 / 4) and 5 trays of sandwiches (25 sandwiches, 1 extra), with clear equations and an explanation of why 5 trays are needed.
Correct number of packs and trays with equations; the explanation is incomplete.
One part correct, or a correct strategy with a calculation error (for example 4 trays).
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 2: Place value and problem solving with units of measure
units.el: Keep a large analog clock and a number line marked every 5 minutes on display; pre-teach "mass", "liquid volume", "estimate", "round" and "elapsed time" with real objects (a 1-liter bottle, a 1-kilogram bag).

lessons.name: Telling time to the minute and elapsed time

practice.q: The hour hand of a clock is just past the 4 and the minute hand points to the 7. What time is it?
practice.h: Each number on the clock stands for 5 minutes. Count by 5s up to the 7.

practice.q: How many minutes are in 1 hour?
practice.h: Think about how long it takes the minute hand to go all the way around the clock.

practice.q: Rosa starts reading at 3:15 p.m. and stops at 3:52 p.m. How many minutes does she read?
practice.h: Count on from 3:15 to 3:50, then add the last few minutes.

practice.q: A movie starts at 6:40 p.m. and lasts 45 minutes. When does it end?
practice.h: How many minutes from 6:40 to 7:00? How many minutes are still left after that?

practice.q: Diego needs 25 minutes to bike to practice. Practice starts at 4:10 p.m. What is the latest time he can leave home?
practice.h: Count back 10 minutes to 4:00, then count back the rest of the 25 minutes.

practice.q: Explain how a number line can help you find the time 28 minutes after 2:45.
practice.ans: Mark 2:45 and jump 15 minutes to 3:00, then jump 13 more minutes to 3:13. The jumps add to 28 minutes, so the time is 3:13.

quiz.q: The hour hand is between the 11 and the 12, and the minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. What time is it?
A bus ride starts at 8:05 a.m. and ends at 8:47 a.m. How many minutes long is the ride?
Priya puts bread in the oven at 10:35 a.m. It bakes for 40 minutes. When does she take it out?
Kenji practices piano for 15 minutes, takes a 5-minute break, then practices 20 more minutes. How many minutes pass from start to finish?
Which time is 17 minutes before 1:05 p.m.?
Lunch starts at 11:50 a.m. Recess comes right after lunch and ends at 12:35 p.m. How many minutes are lunch and recess together?
Omar says the time from 9:40 to 10:10 is 70 minutes because 1010 - 940 = 70. Explain his mistake and give the correct elapsed time.
quiz.ans: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so you cannot subtract the times like whole numbers. From 9:40 to 10:00 is 20 minutes and from 10:00 to 10:10 is 10 minutes, so the elapsed time is 30 minutes.

lessons.name: Measuring mass and liquid volume in metric units

practice.q: Which unit is best for measuring the mass of a paper clip?
practice.h: A paper clip is very light. Which unit is used for light things?

practice.q: Which is the best estimate for the water in a full bathtub?
practice.h: A large water bottle holds about 1 liter. Would one bottle fill a bathtub?

practice.q: A pitcher holds 4 liters of lemonade. Mr. Chen makes 6 pitchers for the school fair. How many liters does he make?
practice.h: Each pitcher is a group of 4 liters.

practice.q: A dog has a mass of 32 kilograms. A puppy has a mass of 9 kilograms. How many kilograms heavier is the dog?
practice.h: "How much heavier" means find the difference.

practice.q: A container is marked 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 liters. The water reaches halfway between the 6 and 8 marks. How much water is in the container?
practice.h: What number is halfway between 6 and 8?

practice.q: One kilogram is the same as 1,000 grams. A bag of rice has a mass of 3 kilograms. How many grams is that?
practice.h: Each kilogram is 1,000 grams. How many groups of 1,000 are there?

quiz.q: Which object has a mass closest to 1 kilogram?
An aquarium holds 36 liters of water. Ava fills it using a 4-liter bucket. How many buckets of water does she pour in?
Three boxes have masses of 14 kilograms, 25 kilograms and 18 kilograms. What is their total mass in kilograms?
A scale shows apples with a mass of 850 grams. Nia adds a 120-gram orange. What does the scale show now?
A jug holds 8 liters of water. Lena pours 3 liters into a plant tub. Then she fills 2 bottles that hold 2 liters each. How many liters are left in the jug?
Which is the best estimate for the water in a full mop bucket?
Jamal says a 5-kilogram bag of potatoes is lighter than a 900-gram bag of carrots because 5 is less than 900. Is he right? Explain.
quiz.ans: No. 5 kilograms is 5,000 grams, which is more than 900 grams. You must compare masses in the same unit.

lessons.name: Rounding to the nearest ten and hundred

practice.q: Round 63 to the nearest ten.
practice.h: Is 63 closer to 60 or to 70?

practice.q: Round 278 to the nearest ten.
practice.h: Which two tens is 278 between?

practice.q: Round 451 to the nearest hundred.
practice.h: Find the halfway point between 400 and 500. Is 451 above or below it?

practice.q: Round 649 to the nearest hundred.
practice.h: Is 649 more or less than the halfway point, 650?

practice.q: Which number rounds to 300 when rounded to the nearest hundred?
practice.h: Any number from 250 up to 349 rounds to 300.

practice.q: Explain how a vertical number line helps you round 735 to the nearest ten.
practice.ans: Put 730 at the bottom, 740 at the top and 735 at the halfway point. 735 is exactly halfway, and halfway numbers round up, so 735 rounds to 740.

quiz.q: Round 84 to the nearest ten.
Round 715 to the nearest hundred.
The library has 386 books about animals. About how many books is that, to the nearest ten?
Which number does NOT round to 500 when rounded to the nearest hundred?
A number rounds to 70 when rounded to the nearest ten. Which could the number be?
Round 995 to the nearest ten.
Mateo rounded 248 to the nearest hundred and got 300. He said, "First I rounded 248 to 250, and 250 rounds to 300." Explain his mistake.
quiz.ans: You must round the original number, not a number you already rounded. 248 is less than 250, the halfway point, so it is closer to 200 and rounds to 200.

lessons.name: Adding and subtracting measurements with the standard algorithm

practice.h: Add the ones first. Do you have enough ones to make a new ten?
There are no tens in 602. Rename 1 hundred as 10 tens first.

practice.q: A truck carries 465 kilograms of sand and then 378 kilograms more. How many kilograms does it carry in all?
practice.h: Line up the hundreds, tens and ones before you add.

practice.q: A water tank holds 500 liters. 236 liters are used. How many liters are left?
practice.h: Rename 5 hundreds as 4 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones.

practice.q: Estimate 412 + 289 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
practice.h: Round each number first, then add the rounded numbers.

practice.q: Explain how you can check that 703 - 468 = 235 is correct.
practice.ans: Add the answer to the number subtracted: 235 + 468 = 703. Since the sum is 703, the subtraction is correct.

quiz.q: A school play sold 286 tickets on Friday and 347 tickets on Saturday. How many tickets were sold in all?
A rope is 950 centimeters long. Ms. Patel cuts off 476 centimeters. How many centimeters long is the rope now?
Which is the best estimate for 689 - 312, rounding each number to the nearest hundred?
A farmer picked 238 kilograms of grapes on Monday and 175 kilograms on Tuesday. She sold 290 kilograms. How many kilograms of grapes does she have left?
Hana solved 504 - 267 and got 363. Explain her mistake and find the correct answer.
quiz.ans: In each place she subtracted the smaller digit from the larger one (7 - 4 and 6 - 0) instead of renaming. She should rename a hundred as tens and a ten as ones. The correct answer is 237.

test.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
Round 537 to the nearest ten.
Round 537 to the nearest hundred.
Which unit is best for measuring the water in a swimming pool?
Art class starts at 1:25 p.m. and ends at 2:10 p.m. How long is art class?
Which number rounds to 600 when rounded to the nearest hundred and to 640 when rounded to the nearest ten?
Which mass is the heaviest?
Ari leaves home at 7:48 a.m. and walks 17 minutes to school. When does Ari arrive?
A water cooler holds 18 liters. Students drink 3 liters from it each hour. How many hours until the cooler is empty?
A bridge can hold 900 kilograms. A car with a mass of 685 kilograms is on it. How many more kilograms can the bridge hold?
Jada ran for 25 minutes, Luis ran for 38 minutes and Kim ran for 19 minutes. How many minutes did they run altogether?
A bakery bag has 1,000 grams of flour. The baker uses 375 grams for a loaf of bread and 248 grams for a batch of rolls. How many grams of flour are left?
Mr. Lopez's class collected 168 kilograms of paper for recycling. Ms. Wong's class collected 59 kilograms more than Mr. Lopez's class. How many kilograms did the two classes collect in all?
Two numbers are each rounded to the nearest hundred, and the rounded numbers add to 700. Which pair could the numbers be?
Each of 3 bags of oranges has a mass of 6 kilograms. What is the total mass?
A pot holds 12 liters of soup. The cook pours equal amounts into 4 containers until the pot is empty. How many liters are in each container?
Which is the best estimate of 523 + 278?
Explain how you know 9:55 a.m. is 15 minutes before 10:10 a.m.
test.ans: From 9:55 to 10:00 is 5 minutes, and from 10:00 to 10:10 is 10 minutes. 5 + 10 = 15 minutes.

test.q: Mai says 1 kilogram of feathers is lighter than 1 kilogram of rocks. Is she right? Explain.
test.ans: She is not right. Both have a mass of 1 kilogram, so their masses are equal. The feathers take up more space, but they are not lighter.

test.q: Leo added 458 + 276 and got 624. Use estimation to show his answer is not reasonable, then find the correct sum.
test.ans: 458 rounds to 500 and 276 rounds to 300, so the sum should be about 800. 624 is too far from 800. The correct sum is 734.

test.q: Room 12 is going on a field trip. The bus leaves school at 8:35 a.m. and the drive to the science center takes 48 minutes. The class stays at the center for exactly 2 hours, then rides 48 minutes back to school. The class brings 3 coolers that each hold 12 liters of water, and students drink 29 liters during the trip. (a) What time does the class arrive at the center? (b) What time does it get back to school? (c) How many liters of water are left? Show your work with number lines or equations and explain each step.
rub: All correct: arrives 9:23 a.m., leaves at 11:23 a.m., back at 12:11 p.m., and 7 liters left (3 x 12 = 36, 36 - 29 = 7), with clear number lines or equations and explanations.
All answers correct with gaps in the work, or one small error with clear work.
About half the parts correct, or a workable strategy with several calculation errors.
Little correct work.

units.name: Module 3: Multiplication and division with units of 0, 1, 6 to 9 and multiples of 10
units.el: Build arrays with counters and post the frame "___ groups of ___ is ___." Pre-teach "factor", "product", "quotient" and "unknown" with a labeled example of each.

lessons.name: Properties of multiplication and units of 6 and 7

practice.h: Think 5 x 7, then add one more group of 7.
Ask yourself: 6 times what number is 48?

practice.q: Which is equal to 7 x 6?
practice.h: The commutative property lets you switch the order of the factors.

practice.q: There are 7 days in a week. How many days are in 9 weeks?
practice.h: You need 9 groups of 7. Try 10 groups of 7 and take one 7 away.

practice.q: n x 6 = 54. What is n?
practice.h: Count by 6s until you reach 54. How many 6s did you count?

practice.q: Show how to break apart 7 x 7 into two easier facts and solve it.

quiz.q: Which expression has the same value as 6 x 8?
A pack of yogurt has 6 cups. Mrs. Okafor buys 7 packs. How many cups of yogurt does she buy?
63 students sit in rows of 7 at an assembly. How many rows are filled?
Which number makes 42 / m = 6 true?
Theo has 4 boxes of 6 crayons and 3 boxes of 7 crayons. How many crayons does he have in all?
Explain why 6 x 7 and 7 x 6 have the same product. Use an array in your answer.
quiz.ans: An array of 6 rows of 7 can be turned to show 7 rows of 6. The number of dots does not change, so both products are 42.

lessons.name: Units of 8 and the associative property

practice.h: 8 is double 4. Find 4 x 6 and double it.
Count by 8s to 72, or think 8 x ? = 72.

practice.q: Which shows 8 x 3 using the associative property?
practice.h: Write 8 as two factors, then group the factors in a different way.

practice.q: An octopus has 8 arms. How many arms do 7 octopuses have?
practice.h: Find 7 groups of 8. You can use 5 eights plus 2 eights.

practice.q: The letter b stands for the number of bags. 8 x b = 40. What is b?
Explain how you can use 2 x 8 to find 4 x 8 and 8 x 8.
practice.ans: 2 x 8 = 16. 4 x 8 is double 2 x 8, so it is 32. 8 x 8 is double 4 x 8, so it is 64.

quiz.q: Which expression equals 8 x 7?
Tickets to the aquarium cost $8 each. How many dollars do 6 tickets cost?
A teacher has 56 markers. She puts 8 markers in each cup. Which equation finds c, the number of cups?
Isla has $50. She buys 4 books that cost $8 each. How many dollars does she have left?
Ruby says 8 x 6 = 46. Show a way to check her answer and find the correct product.
quiz.ans: 8 x 6 = 4 x 6 + 4 x 6 = 24 + 24 = 48. Ruby's answer is 2 too small; the correct product is 48.

lessons.name: Units of 9 and patterns in the multiplication table

practice.h: Find 10 x 4, then take away one group of 4.
What number times itself is 81?

practice.q: Look at 9 x 2 = 18, 9 x 3 = 27 and 9 x 4 = 36. Which pattern is true?
ch: The digits of each product add to 9
The ones digit goes up by 1
The tens digit goes down by 1
practice.h: Add the tens digit and the ones digit of each product.

practice.q: A bike rack holds 9 bikes. How many bikes fit in 6 racks?
practice.h: Try 10 x 6, then subtract 6.

practice.q: 9 x n = 63. What is n?
practice.h: Count by 9s to 63, or think about which fact of 9 has a product of 63.

practice.q: Explain how 10 x 7 helps you find 9 x 7.
practice.ans: 10 x 7 = 70. 9 x 7 is one group of 7 less than 10 x 7, so 70 - 7 = 63.

quiz.q: A theater has 9 rows with 8 seats in each row. How many seats are there?
Ms. Kim has 54 stickers. She gives 9 stickers to each student. How many students get stickers?
Which number is NOT a product of 9 and a whole number?
A pet store has 3 tanks with 9 fish in each tank. It sells 8 fish. How many fish are left?
Ken says 9 x 6 = 64. Use a pattern or another fact to explain why his answer cannot be correct, and give the correct product.
quiz.ans: For the 9s facts up to 9 x 10, the digits of each product add to 9, but 6 + 4 = 10. Also 10 x 6 = 60 and 60 - 6 = 54, so 9 x 6 = 54.

lessons.name: Units of 0 and 1 and two-step word problems

practice.h: 0 groups of 8 means there are no groups at all.
Put 7 objects into 1 group. How many are in that group?

practice.q: Which equation is true?
practice.h: Test each equation with counters or a drawing.

practice.q: Ella buys 3 packs of 6 juice boxes. Her family drinks 5 juice boxes. How many juice boxes are left?
practice.h: First find how many juice boxes she bought. Then subtract.

practice.q: Mr. Diaz has 4 shelves with 7 books on each shelf. He gets 9 more books. Let b be the total number of books. What is b?
practice.h: Find 4 x 7 first, then add the new books.

practice.q: Explain why any number divided by 1 is that same number.
practice.ans: Dividing by 1 means putting everything into 1 group, so all the objects end up in that group. The group has the same number you started with.

quiz.q: Which is true about 5 x 0 and 0 x 5?
A class of 24 students forms teams of 6. Each team gets 3 balls. How many balls are needed?
Carla earns $7 each week for chores. After 6 weeks she spends $15. How many dollars does she have left?
Which situation can be solved with the equation 5 x 8 - 6 = n?
ch: 5 boxes of 8 pencils, and 6 pencils are given away
